title: Error landscape map and trace-bridge for cross-service failure attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build an "error landscape" map + a "trace-bridge" integration that ties model-serving spans to downstream application faults so engineers can quickly attribute customer-facing errors (timeouts, overload, model failures, HTTP/gRPC codes) to the root cause in the inference stack. The ticket scopes the span/attribute schema, collection pipeline changes, a prototype Grafana dashboard (Error Landscape Map), and runbook additions for SREs and on-call. This is focused on cross-service attribution: routing, batching, KV cache behavior, model variant fallbacks, and client HTTP/gRPC surface. Deliverables include instrumentation changes for Go/Python SDKs, OTLP trace enrichment, aggregated error event table, and the dashboard with causal-path visualization and recovery metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-bridge end-to-end: a request that hits the runtime and triggers a model error or timeout appears as a connected trace across API gateway -> routing -> runtime -> model process in Tempo and links to an aggregated error event in ClickHouse/metrics store

Span schema published in a docs page with required fields: request_id, trace_id, model_id, model_variant, batch_id, seq_len, kv_cache_hit (boolean), kernel_path, upstream_status_code, downstream_status_code, latency_ms
Grafana Error Landscape Map prototype shows top 5 causal chains, time-to-detect, time-to-recover, and per-chain customer impact scoring
Automated tests for instrumentation (unit for attribute presence; integration smoke that simulates model timeouts) are green in CI
On-call runbook updated with playbook entries for each failure class (timeout, overload, model-error, auth/network) and links to dashboard filters
implementation_notes: We will reuse OpenTelemetry/OTLP as the collector protocol. Instrumentation work split across: (a) runtime code: add span events when batch is assembled, KV cache lookup result, kernel selection, model-call start/end; (b) public SDKs: propagate traceparent and attach redwood.request.* attributes; (c) gateway/router: map HTTP/gRPC status codes to canonical failure classes and emit short-lived error-events to ClickHouse. Aggregation: add a lightweight error-event schema in ClickHouse for fast group-bys; store a pointer (trace_id) to full trace in Tempo. Visualization: Grafana panel uses traces for causal path and ClickHouse for counts/latency heatmaps. Rollout: start with opt-in flag for 10% of traffic, monitor overhead. Key trade-offs: additional span attributes increase payload size; we will make some attributes optional behind a feature flag. Kernel-level instrumentation will be minimal to avoid jitter in p95 latency.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed for tag schema and collector throughput — observed ~1.6% additional payload overhead when adding model_variant and kv_cache_hit attributes (notes in confluence).
2025-02-18: Prototype OTLP pipeline validated (local Tempo + ClickHouse) using synthetic traces from load generator; initial dashboard panels mocked in Grafana (see links).
2025-02-24: Runtime PR opened GH-5912 with span events for batch lifecycle and KV cache boolean; unit tests added but integration tests failing in CI due to missing collector config.

2025-03-02: Collector config PR merged to infra repo GH-5998; integration smoke tests passing on staging with 5% sample traffic. Latency overhead measured at +0.9% p95 in staging on n2-standard nodes.
review_feedback: PM (R. Alvarez) requested clearer customer impact scoring for the dashboard — added a formula that combines request volume, error rate delta, and affected tenant weight.
Design (S. Kim) suggested colorblind-friendly palette and a compact causal-path view to avoid overwhelming SRE on-call screens.
Security requested a short data retention review: we will keep full traces (with attributes) for 7 days and aggregated error-events for 90 days; sensitive fields will be redacted at collector.
Infra review recommended sampling strategy: 100% for errors, 5% for success traces, and 1% for high-throughput endpoints.
qa_plan: Stage tests: run synthetic scenarios that exercise each failure class (model timeout, model exception, router overload, client gRPC CANCELLED) and assert: (1) trace links exist across components, (2) aggregated error-event shows correct canonical failure class, (3) dashboard filters surface the trace_id. Performance test: run a 30m load window comparing baseline vs instrumented binary and ensure p95 overhead < 2%.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in) 5% traffic with collector sampling at 100% errors; Phase 2 25% after 72h of stability; Phase 3 100% for internal clusters and 20% for external tenants for 2 weeks. Feature flags: redwood.observability.trace_bridge and redwood.observability.kv_tagging. If p95 latency regression > 1.5% or error telemetry ingestion cost exceeds budget, rollback to previous flag state.
follow_up: Create a lightweight nightly job that recomputes the 'top causal chains' table for the dashboard (ENG-74890 placeholder)
Add SDK decorators to automatically redact PII from model prompts in spans (security follow-up)
Run an on-call postmortem playbook tabletop with SRE and product to validate runbook efficacy (schedule in Cycle 42)
